name: Bangladesh
notes: Depth: seed pass R001 and second pass R002 (2026-11-11). Scope: national debate only, in English and Bengali; some Bengali outlets (Bangla Tribune, Dhaka Tribune, Jagonews, Risingbd, Dhaka Post, Jamuna) answer 403 to scripts. Geography: Bangladesh G0001, Jatiya Sangsad G0002, 8 divisions and 64 districts from the OCHA COD-AB Bangladesh dataset (CC BY-IGO 3.0, BBS boundaries, P-codes BD10 to BD60 and BD1004 to BD6094). The local tier is the district (zila); the 495 upazilas (OCHA admin 3) are not loaded. No standalone wealth tax exists: the Wealth Tax Act of 1963 was repealed in 1999 and replaced from FY2011-12 by a surcharge of 10% to 35% on income tax payable for net wealth above Tk 4 crore. In May 2026 the NBR drafted a direct tax of 0.25% to 1% on declared net wealth above Tk 4 crore to replace the surcharge; the Prime Minister dropped it before the 11 June 2026 budget. Supporters found (R001 and R002) are economists and think tanks, a professional body of economists, the interim government's task force, the tax authority and its chairman, a former finance minister, a former NBR member, one Jamaat-e-Islami MP who spoke in the June 2026 budget debate, one line in the BNP manifesto, and columnists. No union, Oxfam, ActionAid, TIB, NCP, Gono Odhikar or left-party statement for a wealth tax was found in pages that could be read. Opponents (Masud Khan, Muhith, Mirza Azizul Islam, Sajjad Zohir, Mamun Rashid) are in exclusions.csv. No Seats tab: parliament.gov.bd did not answer, so no Jatiya Sangsad member list was read.
